uniequip_002_tanya:
Tanya lifted the last of the wounded down from the handcart, then slumped onto the muddy ground. More than ten hours had passed since they pulled out of Zelgrad, and the sound of shellfire had long since faded away.
Crownslayer appeared behind Tanya, weariness on her face, and looked at the sheet-metal bucket on the handcart, the one Tanya had made herself, and the empty detergent canisters filling it to the brim.
'You told Red earlier there wasn't a scrap of room left on that cart. He carried five kids on his back the whole way.'
'This bucket is something I have to bring with me.' Tanya said. 'You talked to Red?'
'Mm. He told me you went and asked about Reunion. So, have you decided? Red would be more than happy to take you in.'
'Still thinking about it.' Tanya paused. 'I was thinking about my sister.'
'Masha, or the little one? I just saw them, they're asleep along with Grisha.' Then it came to Crownslayer. 'Oh. You mean...'
'Nina.'
Crownslayer sat down.
'Those are all detergent canisters I emptied out myself.' Tanya said. 'When I was little, my parents used this same brand. There were piles of them at home, and they were the whole of my toy collection. They used to be Nina's favorite toys, too.'
'I saw a lot of split gashes on them. You used the canisters as training targets?'
'Mm. But they were supposed to be toys.'
'And the bucket?'
'It was supposed to hold water, or cystymilk. Supposed to keep people alive. Then I started training myself, and I used it to wash the blood out of cloth. And after that...' Tanya drew a bundle of white cloth from the bottom of the iron bucket. She unwrapped it, revealing a handful of bone-white ashes. 'I thought about keeping Nina's swaddling cloth, but in the end I burned it.'
Tanya gazed at that harmless handful of ash for a long while. Flame runs like water, rinsing every filth and every sin away.
'From beginning to end, all I ever wanted was for a child to be a child, for a toy to be a toy, and for a bucket to be just a bucket, and nothing else.'
Crownslayer shook her head. 'That's too hard. Turning this whole land upside down would probably be easier.'
'Then at the very least, I want to hold on to my own life.' Tanya looked steadily into Crownslayer's eyes. 'But Zelgrad's gone now. At a time like this, isn't it a little shameful for someone to think only of her own life?'
'Everyone will have their own opinion.' Crownslayer said. 'If you're asking me, I think facing your own life head-on takes a great deal of courage.'
'So it isn't shameful.' Tanya nodded.
'Time to rest, Tanya. There's more road tomorrow.'
'Wait. I heard Rhodes Island gives medical priority to Infected children. Is that true?'
'Not just children. With an infection like yours, you could actually apply to Rhodes Island for operator status or something of the sort. It'd take a lot of the weight off your life.' Crownslayer flicked her eyes toward the loosened bandage on Tanya's arm, and only then did Tanya notice that the black stone she had kept hidden for so long had somehow slipped into view.
'This bandage needs a wash.' Tanya murmured to herself, and then it occurred to her that perhaps, from now on, she would no longer need bandages to hide anything at all.
